title: Pacific Coast Highway
subtitle: San Francisco → Los Angeles
summary: Three slow days down Highway 1: sea cliffs in Big Sur, elephant seals, Santa Barbara wine and a sunset finish in Santa Monica.

days.title: Fog, cliffs & Carmel
days.summary: Leave the city early and ease into coast mode with tide pools and a cozy Carmel dinner.

stops.title: Breakfast at Tartine Manufactory
stops.description: Morning buns and coffee before hitting the road.

stops.title: Pigeon Point Lighthouse
stops.description: One of the tallest lighthouses on the West Coast, right on the cliffs.
stops.tips: Walk to the north side of the parking lot for the classic shot.

stops.title: 17-Mile Drive
stops.description: Scenic loop through Pebble Beach — Lone Cypress, Bird Rock and crashing surf.
stops.tips: Pay the toll at the Pacific Grove gate.

days.title: Big Sur, the main event
days.summary: The most dramatic stretch of coastline in California. No signal for long stretches — download maps!

stops.title: Bixby Creek Bridge
stops.whyVisit: The most photographed spot on Highway 1, and the gateway to Big Sur.
stops.about: A 1932 concrete arch bridge spanning a 280-ft-deep canyon where the creek meets the Pacific.
highlights: North-side pullout for the postcard shot
Old Coast Road dirt track view

stops.title: Fuel up in Big Sur Village
stops.tips: Last reasonably priced gas for ~100 km.

stops.title: McWay Falls
stops.whyVisit: One of the only waterfalls in the world that pours straight onto an ocean beach.
stops.about: An 80-ft waterfall in Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park that drops into a turquoise cove. The beach itself is off-limits, which keeps it untouched.
stops.description: Walk the short Overlook Trail for the classic view, then sit on the bench and take it in.

stops.title: Lunch at Nepenthe
stops.whyVisit: Lunch 800 ft above the ocean at a Big Sur institution since 1949.
stops.about: A family-run restaurant on land once owned by Orson Welles and Rita Hayworth, famous for its cliffside terrace.
stops.tips: Ask for a terrace table — the view is the whole point.

stops.title: Hearst Castle
stops.whyVisit: A jaw-dropping hilltop palace built by the newspaper tycoon William Randolph Hearst.
stops.about: A 165-room estate filled with European art and antiques, built between 1919 and 1947 and now a state historic park.
highlights: Zebras grazing along the highway below

stay.name: Madonna Inn
stay.about: A kitschy, pink, one-of-a-kind roadside icon since 1958 — every room has its own wild theme.
stay.address: 100 Madonna Rd, San Luis Obispo, CA
stay.notes: Famously wild themed rooms. Grab pink champagne cake at the bakery.

stops.title: Santa Barbara Funk Zone
stops.whyVisit: The most fun way to taste Santa Barbara wine without driving to the vineyards.
stops.about: A few walkable blocks of old warehouses turned into wine tasting rooms, breweries, galleries and street art.
stops.description: Wander, taste a couple of local wines, and grab tacos a block from the beach.

stops.title: Sunset at Santa Monica Pier
stops.tips: Park at Lot 1 North, then walk the beach path.

checklist.text: Download offline maps for Big Sur
